newsitem.title: USA: USDA may cut U.S. corn export estimate - analysts.
newsitem.headline: USDA may cut U.S. corn export estimate - analysts.

text.p: A recent pickup in the U.S. corn export pace may not be enough to prevent the U.S. Department of Agriculture from cutting its estimate for 1996/97 when it issues its Supply/Demand report next week, analysts said.
"There is too much competition from Argentina. We're not keeping up with the (USDA) pace. I'm surprised they didn't do it last month," said Dean Witter analyst Jerry Gidel.
Gidel said he expected USDA to cut its estimate of corn exports in 1996/97 (September/August) by 50 to 75 million bushels, prompting a similar hike in ending stocks.
Some analysts said USDA may wait a little longer to see how corn exports develop before making a cut.
"I don't think they will lower it (corn exports) just yet, said analyst Mickey Luth of LaiFa Group. But he said he had already cut 50 million bushels off his own estimate.
Analyst Joel Karlin, of Everen Securities, noted the recent increased export pace may have delayed any cut.

"My corn export number is actually a bit lower (than the USDA) but I think the pace of corn exports has been very strong recently so there might not be an adjustment there," said Everen Securities Joel Karlin.
Karlin's current export estimate of 1.85 billion bushels is slightly below USDA's January projection of 1.90 billion.
Analysts said little change was expected in wheat supply/demand data, with the outlook for Australian production possibly the main focus in that market.

"There is not much change in the domestic situation, but we should have an upward adjustment for Australia. It seems likely and logical they will bump it up a million (tonnes)," Karlin of Everen Securities said.
Last month USDA put Australian wheat output at 21.50 million tonnes.
Much higher estimates have circulated since then. The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) put the crop at 23.116 million earlier this month.

USDA was expected to keep unchanged its estimate of Argentine wheat production of 15.50 million tonnes, although a slight downward revision appears possible after recent rains diminished crop potential, analysts said.
